title: VPC observability lifecycle Terraform module (Prometheus/Grafana + OTEL + log shippers)
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a single opinionated Terraform module to provision and manage the VPC observability stack for Private deployments. The module will create Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), an OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) + receivers/exporters, and log-shipping components (Fluent Bit -> S3/Vector -> LogForwarder). It must include safe lifecycle and upgrade hooks, automated health checks for each component, canary upgrade support, and outputs/inputs for integration with the Private control plane and Redbox (routing).

Scope and constraints:
- Must be usable in customer VPCs (private subnets, NAT or no NAT), with configurable networking (service CIDR, SGs, NACLs).
- Support both Helm (for Grafana/Prom) and native k8s manifests for OTEL and log shippers depending on customer air-gap constraints.
- Provide Terraform-level lifecycle hooks for rolling upgrades and drain: pre-upgrade hook to scale down forwarders, post-upgrade smoke tests, and optional canary rollout percentage.
- Health checks exposed as k8s readiness/liveness for pods + a module-level health endpoint (Route53 private alias + ALB targets) to be polled by our Upgrade Orchestrator.
- Backwards-compatible variables and sensible defaults to avoid breaking existing customers when the module is bumped.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Module can deploy a full stack in an isolated test VPC and pass automated integration tests (see testing_plan).
- Terraform plan/apply does not recreate resources for minor module bumps when features are toggled off.
- Canary upgrade path available (example: upgrade 10% of Prometheus replicas, validate metrics scrape, then continue).
- Healthcheck endpoints return success within 60s after successful rollout and produce meaningful failure messages on failure.
- Module exposes outputs for Prometheus endpoint, Grafana URL, OTel collector endpoint, and log-forwarder S3 bucket ARN.

Notes on backward compatibility:
- Use versioned Helm charts and pin defaults to known-good chart versions. Introduce new features behind boolean flags (e.g., enable_remote_storage) to avoid surprise diffs.
- Add migration guide in Confluence if we change storage layout or PV provisioner.

Implementation patterns and variables (non-exhaustive):
- Variables: cluster_name, vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, prometheus_retention_days, grafana_admin_password_secret_arn, otel_config_map_override, enable_canary, canary_percent, log_shipper_backend (s3|vector|cloudwatch), healthcheck_alb_enabled, public_access (disabled by default).
- Outputs: prometheus_scrape_endpoint, grafana_url, otel_ingest_endpoint, log_shipper_bucket, module_version
- Use Terraform 1.5+ features: for_each with maps for component toggles, lifecycle ignore_changes for chart app annotations where we expect autoscaler to modify replicas, and external data provider for smoke tests where necessary.

Migration/upgrade considerations:
- Provide a test target workspace for upgrades that runs 'plan' and a synthetic canary apply to validate no destructive changes.
- Add a tool to diff chart values and highlight fields that will force resource replacement (PVCs, storageClass changes).

Operational concerns:
- Cost controls: default small node selector requests for Prom/Grafana; document recommended sizing for production.
- Observability of the observability stack: the module should emit a module-health metric to our global telemetry (via OTLP exporter) when deployed in Private accounts.

Example usage snippet (HCL):
module "obs_stack" {
  source = "git::ssh://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//observability/vpc-stack?ref=obs-module-2026.03"
  cluster_name = "customer-123-prod"
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  private_subnet_ids = var.private_subnet_ids
  prometheus_retention_days = 14
  grafana_admin_password_secret_arn = data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.graf_creds.arn
  enable_canary = true
  canary_percent = 10
  log_shipper_backend = "s3"
}
acceptance_criteria: Deploy completes in CI in under 15 minutes for a minimal test cluster
Module outputs include prometheus_scrape_endpoint, grafana_url, otel_ingest_endpoint, and log_shipper_bucket
Canary upgrade runs successfully and automatically promotes after health checks pass
No destructive replacements caused by default variable changes
Healthcheck ALB returns 200 within 60s of post-upgrade smoke test
implementation_notes: Keep Helm providers optional to support air-gapped installs via local chart tarballs
Expose a lightweight 'smoke' test binary executed by CI that hits /metrics, /-/healthy for Prom and /api/health for Grafana
Encapsulate log-shipping policy as a single configurable block with backends and retention policies
Use Terraform workspaces to separate 'canary' and 'stable' upgrades during test runs
testing_plan: CI blueprint: spin up k3s cluster in CI runner, apply module with minimal values, run smoke tests (smoke binary + OTLP ingestion verification)
Integration test: deploy to staging VPC, run full e2e: scrape verification, dashboard provisioning via Grafana API, log ingestion and S3 lifecycle validation
Upgrade test: run module version bump in staging with enable_canary=true and verify canary promotion logic via automated health checks
Chaos test: simulate node replacement and ensure readiness/liveness and module health metric remains (or degrades gracefully)
rollout_plan: Week 1: merge module skeleton + basic Prom/Grafana/OTel manifests behind flags. Deploy to internal test VPC.
Week 2: add Helm charts, log-shipping backends, and health ALB. Run full CI and integration tests.
Week 3: run guided canary upgrades in staging with operators and document rollout playbook.
Week 4: tag 2026.03 release and publish migration notes + upgrade guide in Confluence
